1: Chapter 1: Visitor on a Rainy Night

In Doldari village, rain had been falling for three days straight. Kim Haneul’s older sister had left for Seoul in the spring, and since then the village’s tiny pharmacy had been run solely by Haneul.
When darkness fell, she closed the side door, counted the money earned that day, put out the oil lamp, and went upstairs.
She had just lain down when a frantic knock came from downstairs, and a man’s voice asked, “Is anyone there?”

At the door stood a young man soaked to the skin. Blood had seeped through the cloth wrapped around his left arm. He introduced himself as Park Junho, saying he was a member of the Azure Dragon Society.
“Please tend to my wound,” Park Junho said quietly. “I’ll pay you. Would 3,500 yang be enough?”
He drew an oil‑paper‑wrapped letter from his bosom. “This letter needs to be sent to Cheongpungsa by May 18.”
Haneul thought to herself, “Just as the neighbors were resentful of the pharmacy doing well, a stranger shows up at midnight.”
Still, Haneul refused the money and said only, “I’ll guide you to the mountains early tomorrow morning.”
2: As soon as dawn broke, the two set out on the road. Haneul carried a basket on her back containing rice balls, herbs, and an old umbrella.

On the mountainside they met an old man, Lee Youngsoo, who was chopping firewood. He lowered his axe and spoke in a low voice: yesterday evening three strangers had been looking for an injured young man at the village entrance.
"Haneul, take the side path," said Lee Youngsoo. "The main road is dangerous." Haneul thanked the old man.
The side path was narrow and slippery. Haneul led the way, stepping firmly with each step. Park Junho followed silently behind.
At noon the rain stopped and the mountain mist slowly lifted, revealing the roof of Cheongpungsa in the distance. A nun stood before the temple gate—Jeonghye, who greeted visitors at the temple.
Jeonghye took the letter, checked the red seal on the envelope, and nodded. "The head monk has been waiting for this letter for two years."
Park Junho said to Haneul, "You saved my life." Haneul smiled and replied, "If you come again, could you fix the pharmacy roof?" Park Junho stayed at the temple.
In the evening Haneul came down the mountain alone. By the time she reached home it was already dark. She lit a lamp and sat for a long time behind the counter.
